# Stario

Stario is a Python framework for server-rendered hypermedia apps. Handlers are async functions that write HTML through a `Writer`. Routes are explicit `Route` values. Datastar morphs the page in the browser. A long-lived SSE stream keeps a screen live. State lives on the server. Stario is not ASGI; run it with `python -m app.main`, or `just dev` / `uv run watchfiles 'python -m app.main' app/ static/` in development.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](https://stario.dev/AGENTS.md): the app guide. Copy it into every Stario repo. Layout, invariants, the CQRS default, render from state, signals, code shape, tests, common mistakes.
- [stario-create](https://github.com/bobowski/stario-create): `uvx stario-create new my-app` creates a runnable app with the guide, the skills, and a `justfile`.
- [llms-full.txt](https://stario.dev/llms-full.txt): the guide and the skills in one file, for tools that want more context.
- [The Stario way](https://stario.dev/docs/explanation/the-stario-way): why Stario is shaped this way.

## Skills (optional stacks)

- [stario-feature](https://stario.dev/skills/stario-feature/SKILL.md): add or remove one screen, step by step.
- [stario-auth](https://stario.dev/skills/stario-auth/SKILL.md): a signed session cookie, `c.state["user"]`, a login screen, protected screens.
- [stario-litewriter](https://stario.dev/skills/stario-litewriter/SKILL.md): SQLite through `litewriter`; `watch` repaints the stream.
- [stario-tailwind-daisyui](https://stario.dev/skills/stario-tailwind-daisyui/SKILL.md): Tailwind v4 and DaisyUI with the standalone binary, no Node.
- [stario-client](https://stario.dev/skills/stario-client/SKILL.md): where JavaScript goes, and how Python calls `app.<name>`.

## Defaults in one paragraph

One folder per screen under `app/features/<screen>/` with `urls.py`, `views.py`, `handlers.py`, and `data.py` when the screen owns tables. A screen whose state cannot change while it is open is one `GET`, plus private reads that patch one part. A screen that shows shared state that can change is `GET /page`, `GET /page/live`, and `POST` commands that reply 204 and publish. One `render(state)` returns the full document; the stream sends it again on each change. Signals carry inputs and client-only state. Tests run through `TestClient(bootstrap)` and read the stream with `iter_events()`. That next event is the live-update check. A Playwright script (in the `stario-feature` skill) checks that Datastar morphed it; a computer-use session is for a look the assertion cannot make.
